exposure: mode of delivery (vaginal delivery vs. cesarean section)
cohort: The study included 88 pregnant women with twin pregnancies at >32 weeks gestation, divided into groups for vaginal delivery (44 women) and cesarean section (44 women).
finding: Cesarean section for the second twin resulted in significantly better Apgar scores at 1 and 5 minutes and higher umbilical artery pH (>7.2) compared to vaginal delivery, and an intertwin delivery interval of >=10 minutes was associated with a low Apgar score.
mod_finding: Cesarean section for the second twin showed significantly better Apgar scores and umbilical artery pH compared to vaginal delivery.
